# On the Pleasure of Small Uncertainties

I've been thinking about how much of life's texture comes from not knowing what comes next.

There's this moment before you open a letter, or before a friend texts back, or when you're walking into a room full of people you've never met—that little gap between expectation and reality. It's uncomfortable, sure, but it's also where something like aliveness lives.

We spend so much energy trying to eliminate uncertainty. We check weather forecasts, read reviews, scroll through photos before visiting somewhere. We want the surprise removed so we can optimize our experience. But I wonder if we're trading something valuable for that comfort.

The best conversations I can remember aren't the ones where I knew exactly what the other person would say. The best books have moments that genuinely surprise me, even on rereading. Even familiar songs can catch me off guard with a particular lyric suddenly landing differently than before.

There's also something almost generous about uncertainty—it means the world isn't fully determined. People can still change their minds. You can still become someone different than you expected. A day that starts badly can veer sideways into something wonderful.

Maybe the trick isn't eliminating uncertainty but getting more comfortable with it. Holding it lightly instead of gripping so hard at the edges.
